Songwriters first. That’s the mission.

WSWS is being built around a pretty simple idea: give songwriters better infrastructure at every stage of their career, and give the people around them better tools to support them.

The app and the industry tools serve different parts of that mission.

The app is for the songwriter who is still finding their crew, building relationships, writing more songs, and trying to create the opportunities that can move their career forward. It gives them a place for their connections, their songs, their splits, and eventually more of the day to day work that comes with being a songwriter.

And one of the things we hear most often from established writers when they see it is some version of:

“I wish I had this when I was getting started.”

That is important context, because we are not expecting a songwriter with decades of relationships and a calendar full of co writes to download WSWS because they need help finding someone to write with.

They have already built their crew.

But their world still matters enormously to what we are building.

That is where the songwriter portals, roster tools, network mapping, data, and other industry products come in. Those are being built for the writers who have reached that level and, just as importantly, for the managers, publishers, coordinators, labels, and teams doing an incredible amount of work behind them every day.

The app helps writers build their world. The portals help established writers and their teams better understand and manage the world they have already built.

And ultimately, both sides make the other stronger.

This is bigger than trying to get every songwriter onto an app. The opportunity is to bring the songwriting community together around infrastructure that actually starts with the people creating the songs.

For established writers, artists, and their teams, that creates a different invitation.

Not “you need this to become successful.” You already are.

It is an opportunity to help shape what exists for the next generation of writers coming behind you, while also building tools that can make life easier for the teams supporting the writers at the highest level today.

Whether someone is trying to find their first real group of co writers, writing their hundredth major cut, or managing the relationships and catalog behind one of the biggest writers in town, they should be able to see themselves somewhere in what WSWS is building.

Because every decision starts with the same question:

Does this make the songwriter’s world better?

For decades, enormous infrastructure has been built around what happens after a song exists. Publishers, labels, PROs, distributors, streaming services, and countless other companies all play important roles.

But the actual creation layer, where writers meet, write, document, organize, and build careers around songs, has never really had a home of its own at global scale.

That is the opportunity for WSWS.

And when that layer gets stronger, everyone benefits.

Better organized writers create cleaner metadata. Better connected writers create more opportunities and more songs. Better tools give teams more time to focus on the creative work and relationships that actually matter. And a stronger network of songwriters gives publishers, labels, managers, and artists a better understanding of where songs, relationships, and talent are developing.

WSWS starts with the writers who have the least infrastructure around them today. But it is being built with the belief that supporting songwriters cannot stop there.

It has to include the people who have already made it. It has to include the teams behind them. And it should give those writers a way to help make the path better for the next group coming up behind them.

Every dollar in this business starts with a song. Every song starts with songwriters.

If we can collectively put them back at the head of the table, the entire music industry gets stronger.
